                ;**********************************************************************
                ; CHRGET ($0073-$008A) - executable code living in zero page, not data.
                ;
                ; The KERNAL copies this 24-byte routine into RAM at power-up; it is BASIC's tokenizer feed. It
                ; increments the 16-bit text pointer at $7A/$7B, fetches the next program byte through an
                ; absolute LDA whose operand IS $7A/$7B (self-modifying by design), skips spaces, and returns
                ; with carry clear when the byte is an ASCII digit.
                ;
                ; Byte-verified against the stock routine:
                ;   E6 7A D0 02 E6 7B AD 06 02 C9 3A B0 0A C9 20 F0 EF 38 E9 30 38 E9 D0 60
                ;
                ; Unmodified and unreachable here: BASIC ROM is banked out ($01 = $36). TXTPTR reads $0206,
                ; pointing into the BASIC input buffer - residue of the RUN that started the game.
                ;**********************************************************************
CHRGET:

0074            7a                        byte      7Ah
0075            d0                        byte      D0h
0076            02                        byte      2h
0077            e6                        byte      E6h

                ;**********************************************************************
                ; KERNAL current-file parameter block ($B2-$C5), the part of zero page the game does write.
                ;
                ;   $B2-$B3  TAPE1   start of the cassette buffer. RESTORE_SYSTEM_TO_BASIC writes $033C here
                ;                    ($A8A8/$A8AC), reproducing what the KERNAL's RAMTAS does at $FD5F
                ;   $B7      FNLEN   filename length
                ;   $B9      SA      secondary address. LOAD_NEXT_GAME_PART writes 0 at $971D, which tells LOAD
                ;                    to place the file at the address in MEMUSS rather than honouring the load
                ;                    address stored in the file's first two bytes
                ;   $BA      FA      device number. $9723 writes 8, the first disk drive
                ;   $BB-$BC  FNADR   filename pointer, normally set through SETNAM ($FFBD)
                ;   $C2      STAL+1  I/O start address high; $A8AE writes $03
                ;   $C3-$C4  MEMUSS  the load address LOAD uses when SA = 0; $971F writes the low byte
                ;   $C5      LSTX    matrix code of the last key SCNKEY saw; $40 = none
                ;
                ; Comparing this block against ZERO_PAGE_BACKUP dates the backup exactly: $A0B7 = 5 and
                ; $A0BB/$A0BC = $9735 are the SETNAM("PART2") parameters written at $9725-$972B, so the backup
                ; half is zero page as LOAD_NEXT_GAME_PART left it.
                ;**********************************************************************
TAPE1_CASSETTE_BUFFER_PTR:
TAPE1_CASSETTE_BUFFER_PTR+1:  ; offcut at 00b3
                ; XREF[1]: a8a8(W)
                ; XREF offcut[1]: a8ac(W)
00b2            0302                      word      203h
00b4            00                        byte      0h
00b5            00                        byte      0h
00b6            00                        byte      0h

                ; KERNAL screen-editor, keyboard and RS-232 workspace ($C7-$FD).                 ; $CB SFDX is the matrix code of the key being scanned; $40 means none. $CC BLNSW disables cursor blink. $D1-$D2 point to screen line $0400. $D5 LNMX is $27 (39). $D6 TBLX is the cursor physical line and is not game state. $D9-$F2 is the 26-byte screen line-link table. $F3-$F4 point to Color RAM $D800; $F5-$F6 point to the KERNAL unshifted keyboard table $EB81; $F7-$FA are null RS-232 buffer pointers. $FD is cleared by LOAD_NEXT_GAME_PART at $971B with the KERNAL file parameters; its consumer is the fast-loader image under I/O at $DC00-$DFFF, outside this snapshot.

                ;**********************************************************************
                ; Live 6510 stack at capture: twelve bytes holding the six nested JSR return addresses of the
                ; documented call chain. No frame of that chain lies below $01F4, which is why $0100-$01E8 is
                ; prior-stage residue rather than active state. JSR stores the address of its final byte, so each
                ; return target is the stored value plus one.
                ;
                ; Innermost first: $01F4=$0554 (JSR $FF9F at $0552, KERNAL SCNKEY); $01F6=$055F (JSR $0552 at
                ; $055D, wait for SPACE); $01F8=$1184 (JSR $055D at $1182); $01FA=$169B (self-modified JSR $117A
                ; at $1699); $01FC=$1578 (JSR $1605 at $1576, bytecode interpreter); $01FE=$0408 (JSR $14D6 at
                ; $0406, INIT_GAME).
                ;
                ; The VSF CPU PC is $EA93 inside KERNAL SCNKEY, reached through $FF9F, matching the innermost
                ; frame. The machine was blocked at the room-setup SPACE prompt.
                ;
                ; Page 1 immediately below $01F4 is not stable: two dumps taken from the same blocked session
                ; differ at $01EC/$01ED, so transient KERNAL and
                ; interrupt frames do reach at least $01EC while the engine waits. Only $01F4-$01FF is asserted.
                ;**********************************************************************

                ;**********************************************************************
                ; RUN_FASTLOADER ($03A0)
                ;
                ; Purpose: Bring the parked custom disk fast-loader into executable space and run it. The image normally lives in the RAM hidden beneath the CIA/I-O window at $DC00-$DFFF; this wrapper exchanges it with the four screen-matrix pages at $CC00-$CFFF and then calls it at $CC00.
                ; Inputs: None in registers. Requires the loader image parked in RAM under $DC00-$DFFF and KERNAL file parameters already set by the caller (LOAD_NEXT_GAME_PART performs SETNAM before calling).
                ; Outputs: The requested part has been loaded by the custom loader; the loader image and the previous screen-matrix contents have been exchanged back by the callee's second half, so $CC00-$CFFF again holds the loader image only for the duration of the call.
                ; Assumptions: Entry with $01=$37 so that KERNAL ROM and the I/O page are visible; the four exchange pages exist both at $CC00-$CFFF and in RAM under $DC00-$DFFF.
                ; Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, plus whatever the custom loader itself uses; the visible screen matrix is destroyed for the duration of the call.
                ; Hardware changes: Indirect: the callee SWAP_FASTLOADER_IMAGE drives the 6510 port $01 between $37 and $38, and the loader itself drives the serial bus on CIA 2 port A ($DD00). The text screen is unreadable while the loader occupies $CC00-$CFFF, which is why the caller blanks the VIC display first.
                ;**********************************************************************
RUN_FASTLOADER:
                ; XREF[1]: 972f(c)
                ; XREF from[1]: 03a0(c)
03a0            20a603                    JSR       SWAP_FASTLOADER_IMAGE  ; Swap the hidden loader into execution space.
                ; XREF from[1]: 03a3(c)
03a3            2000cc                    JSR       SCREEN_RAM  ; Execute the custom loader now resident at $CC00.
                ;**********************************************************************
                ; SWAP_FASTLOADER_IMAGE ($03A6)
                ;
                ; Purpose: Exchange the four 256-byte pages at $CC00-$CFFF with the four pages of RAM that lie underneath the I/O window at $DC00-$DFFF, so that a program parked in hidden RAM becomes executable and the displaced screen matrix is preserved.
                ; Inputs: None in registers. Requires four consecutive pages at $CC00 and four underneath $DC00.
                ; Outputs: The two four-page regions have swapped contents. All four self-modified absolute operand high bytes ($03AD, $03B0, $03B3, $03B7) are reset to $CC/$DC so the routine is re-entrant across calls. Returns with interrupts disabled.
                ; Assumptions: Entry with $01=$37. The routine reaches $38 by INC $01, which is only correct from $37; it restores by DEC $01. Interrupts must stay off while I/O is hidden, otherwise an IRQ acknowledging $D019 would write RAM instead.
                ; Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, the four operand bytes named above, and the interrupt-disable flag (left set on return).
                ; Hardware changes: Executes SEI. Changes the 6510 on-chip port $01 from $37 to $38, which unmaps the whole I/O page (VIC-II, SID, CIAs, colour RAM) and exposes the RAM beneath it, then restores $37. No device register is written.
                ;**********************************************************************
SWAP_FASTLOADER_IMAGE:
                ; XREF[1]: 03a0(c)
03a6            78                        SEI
                ; XREF from[1]: 03a7(RW)
03a7            e601                      INC       MEMORY_MAP_CONFIG  ; Increment $01 from $37 to $38: expose RAM at $D000-$DFFF.
03a9            a200                      LDX       #0x0
SWAP_FASTLOADER_PAGE_LOOP:
SWAP_SRC_VISIBLE_PAGE:  ; offcut at 03ad
                ; XREF[2]: 03b9(j), 03cc(j)
                ; XREF offcut[2]: 03bb(RW), 03d2(W)
                ; XREF from[3]: 03ab(R), 03ab(R), 03ab(R)
03ab            bc00cc                    LDY       SCREEN_RAM,X  ; Read one byte from the visible $CCxx page; operand high byte advances per page.
SWAP_SRC_HIDDEN_PAGE:  ; offcut at 03b0
                ; XREF offcut[2]: 03be(RW), 03da(W)
03ae            bd00dc                    LDA       0xdc00,X  ; Read the corresponding byte from RAM hidden beneath I/O.
SWAP_DST_VISIBLE_PAGE:  ; offcut at 03b3
                ; XREF offcut[2]: 03c1(RW), 03d5(W)
                ; XREF from[3]: 03b1(W), 03b1(W), 03b1(W)
03b1            9d00cc                    STA       SCREEN_RAM,X  ; Move hidden-RAM byte into the $CCxx loader page.
03b4            98                        TYA
SWAP_DST_HIDDEN_PAGE:  ; offcut at 03b7
                ; XREF offcut[3]: 03c4(RW), 03c7(R), 03dd(W)
03b5            9d00dc                    STA       0xdc00,X  ; Store former $CCxx byte under I/O, completing the swap.
03b8            e8                        INX
                ; XREF from[1]: 03b9(j)
03b9            d0f0                      BNE       SWAP_FASTLOADER_PAGE_LOOP
                ; XREF from[1]: 03bb(RW)
03bb            eead03                    INC       SWAP_SRC_VISIBLE_PAGE  ; Advance the $CCxx read operand to the next page.
                ; XREF from[1]: 03be(RW)
03be            eeb003                    INC       SWAP_SRC_HIDDEN_PAGE  ; Advance the $DCxx read operand to the next page.
                ; XREF from[1]: 03c1(RW)
03c1            eeb303                    INC       SWAP_DST_VISIBLE_PAGE  ; Advance the $CCxx write operand to the next page.
                ; XREF from[1]: 03c4(RW)
03c4            eeb703                    INC       SWAP_DST_HIDDEN_PAGE  ; Advance the $DCxx write operand to the next page.
                ; XREF from[1]: 03c7(R)
03c7            adb703                    LDA       SWAP_DST_HIDDEN_PAGE
03ca            c9e0                      CMP       #0xe0  ; Stop after swapping through page $DF.
                ; XREF from[1]: 03cc(j)
03cc            d0dd                      BNE       SWAP_FASTLOADER_PAGE_LOOP
                ; XREF from[1]: 03ce(RW)
03ce            c601                      DEC       MEMORY_MAP_CONFIG  ; Restore $01 from $38 to $37 so ROM and I/O are visible again.
03d0            a9cc                      LDA       #0xcc  ; Reset all self-modified operand high bytes for the next invocation.
                ; XREF from[1]: 03d2(W)
03d2            8dad03                    STA       SWAP_SRC_VISIBLE_PAGE
                ; XREF from[1]: 03d5(W)
03d5            8db303                    STA       SWAP_DST_VISIBLE_PAGE
03d8            a9dc                      LDA       #0xdc
                ; XREF from[1]: 03da(W)
03da            8db003                    STA       SWAP_SRC_HIDDEN_PAGE
                ; XREF from[1]: 03dd(W)
03dd            8db703                    STA       SWAP_DST_HIDDEN_PAGE
03e0            60                        RTS

                ;**********************************************************************
                ; ENTRY_POINT ($0400)
                ;
                ; Purpose: Resident handoff from the excluded startup/intro occupant into gameplay. The two calls at $0400 and $0403 enter excluded byte ranges; the retained boundary fact is that the chain returns at $0406 with the gameplay display, raster IRQ and banking installed. $0406 then initialises the adventure and falls through into the command loop.
                ; Inputs: None in registers. Requires the expanded gameplay image resident in RAM as captured.
                ; Outputs: Gameplay display, IRQ vector and banking installed; adventure state initialised by INIT_GAME; control enters MAIN_LOOP and never returns.
                ; Assumptions: The captured 64 KiB image and an otherwise normal C64. The excluded callees at $069B and $1580 are provenance only; the only asserted contract is that they return with the gameplay display installed.
                ; Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and effectively the whole engine zero page and state block through callees.
                ; Hardware changes: Through the excluded chain and ENTER_GAMEPLAY_DISPLAY: the 6510 port $01, VIC-II display and interrupt registers, SID, colour RAM, and the KERNAL RAM IRQ vector CINV at $0314/$0315.

                ;**********************************************************************
                ; CALL_INIT_GAME ($0406)
                ;
                ; Purpose: Alternate, non-returning entry into game initialisation. Reached by the restart path (JMP from RESTART_GAME at $0FEE). Calls INIT_GAME to rebuild adventure state and the starting room, then falls through into MAIN_LOOP.
                ; Inputs: None in registers.
                ; Outputs: Adventure state rebuilt and the starting room described; control continues in MAIN_LOOP. Never returns to its caller.
                ; Assumptions: The gameplay memory layout, banking, raster IRQ and display are already established; only the adventure state is rebuilt.
                ; Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and all game state through callees. Any stack frame belonging to the abandoned command is not unwound here; RESTART_GAME has already discarded it.
                ; Hardware changes: None directly. Callees write screen and colour RAM through the terminal.
                ;**********************************************************************
CALL_INIT_GAME:
                ; XREF[2]: 01fe(*), 0fee(j)
                ; XREF from[1]: 0406(c)

                ;**********************************************************************
                ; MAIN_LOOP ($0409)
                ;
                ; Purpose: The non-returning foreground command loop: describe the current room, read one edited command line, parse and execute it, repeat forever.
                ; Inputs: None in registers. Requires valid captured PART1 tables and initialised game state.
                ; Outputs: Continuously updated screen and game-state arrays. Never returns; the only exits are the non-local ones taken by RESTART_GAME and ACTION_NEXT_PART.
                ; Assumptions: Runs under the already-established gameplay banking ($01=$36), the raster-split IRQ, and the split display; it does not configure them itself.
                ; Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and the whole parser, VM and renderer workspace.
                ; Hardware changes: None directly; callees write screen RAM at $CC00-$CFFF, colour RAM at $D800-$DBFF, and read the CIA 1 keyboard matrix through KERNAL SCNKEY/GETIN.
                ;**********************************************************************

                ; XREF from[1]: 0412(j)

                ;**********************************************************************
                ; SWITCH_TO_NEXT_PART ($0415)
                ;
                ; Purpose: Advance the multipart overlay selector and bring in the next story part.                 ; Inputs: CURRENT_PART_NO ($2940) valid; the replacement disk part available in the drive.
                ; Outputs: CURRENT_PART_NO incremented, CURRENT_ROOM set, the captured overlay replaced on disk load, LOADED_PART_NO ($5E) recorded, and control transferred to MAIN_LOOP. Non-returning with respect to the action handler that invoked it.
                ; Assumptions: Called only from ACTION_NEXT_PART, which has already discarded three levels of return address, so the stack is at the main-loop level. The replacement occupant's internals are outside this project.
                ; Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, UI and disk scratch, and every array the replacement occupant's initialisation script writes.
                ; Hardware changes: Through its callees: VIC-II display enable and border/background, VIC interrupt enable $D01A, CIA 1 timer A control $DC0E and interrupt control $DC0D, the serial bus, and the 6510 port $01.
                ;**********************************************************************

                ;**********************************************************************
                ; DISK_LOAD_GAME ($0461)

                ; WAIT_FOR_KEY ($0552)

                ;
                ; Purpose: The gameplay-side half of the phase transition: set up the text cursor, clear the text screen, install the runtime disk loader over the excluded title-stage occupant, capture the live bitmap into the packed display buffer, restore the composed display, and install the raster-split IRQ handler.

                ;**********************************************************************
                ; MEMCPY ($0779)
                ;
                ; Purpose: General forward block copy of X complete pages plus an optional Y-byte tail, used for the display bundle, screen scrolling and buffer restores.
                ; Inputs: MEMCPY_SOURCE ($0A/$0B) = source, WORK_PTR ($0C/$0D) = destination, X = number of whole 256-byte pages, Y = tail length in bytes.
                ; Outputs: The requested bytes are copied. The two pointer low bytes are unchanged; their high bytes have been incremented by the original X. When the tail was non-zero the routine returns with Y equal to the tail length.
                ; Assumptions: The copy is strictly forward and does not handle overlapping ranges where the destination is above the source within the same page.                 ; Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, SCRATCH_BYTE_2 ($04), the high bytes of both pointers, and the immediate operand byte at $079E, which retains the most recent non-zero tail length.
                ; Hardware changes: None of its own; the destination may be colour RAM or VIC-visible RAM depending on the caller.
                ;**********************************************************************
MEMCPY:
                ; XREF[6]: 0757(c), 07b6(c), 07cd(c), 07e4(c), 091f(c), 0936(c)
                ; XREF from[1]: 0779(W)
0779            8404                      STY       SCRATCH_BYTE_2  ; Preserve the requested tail length in zero-page scratch $04.
077b            e000                      CPX       #0x0  ; Skip the full-page loop when X is zero.
                ; XREF from[1]: 077d(j)
077d            f010                      BEQ       COPY_REMAINDER_BYTES
077f            a000                      LDY       #0x0

                ; XREF[2]: 0786(j), 078d(j)
                ; XREF from[4]: 0781(R), 0781(R), 0781(R), 0781(R)
0781            b10a                      LDA       (MEMCPY_SOURCE),Y  ; Load through the source pointer.
                ; XREF from[4]: 0783(R), 0783(W), 0783(W), 0783(W)
0783            910c                      STA       (WORK_PTR),Y  ; Store through the destination pointer.
0785            c8                        INY
                ; XREF from[1]: 0786(j)
0786            d0f9                      BNE       COPY_BLOCK_LOOP
                ; XREF from[1]: 0788(RW)
0788            e60b                      INC       MEMCPY_SOURCE+1  ; Advance source pointer by one page.
                ; XREF from[1]: 078a(RW)
078a            e60d                      INC       WORK_PTR+1  ; Advance destination pointer by one page.
078c            ca                        DEX
                ; XREF from[1]: 078d(j)
078d            d0f2                      BNE       COPY_BLOCK_LOOP
COPY_REMAINDER_BYTES:
                ; XREF[1]: 077d(j)
                ; XREF from[1]: 078f(R)
078f            a404                      LDY       SCRATCH_BYTE_2  ; Recover the requested tail length.
                ; XREF from[1]: 0791(j)
0791            f00e                      BEQ       COPY_COMPLETED
                ; XREF from[1]: 0793(W)
0793            8c9e07                    STY       REMAINDER_BYTES  ; Patch the CPY immediate operand with the tail length.
0796            a000                      LDY       #0x0

                ; XREF from[3]: 0798(R), 0798(R), 0798(R)
0798            b10a                      LDA       (MEMCPY_SOURCE),Y  ; Copy the remaining partial page.
                ; XREF from[3]: 079a(R), 079a(W), 079a(W)
079a            910c                      STA       (WORK_PTR),Y
079c            c8                        INY
REMAINDER_BYTES:  ; offcut at 079e
                ; XREF offcut[1]: 0793(W)
079d            c080                      CPY       #0x80  ; Self-modified tail-loop bound.
                ; XREF from[1]: 079f(j)
079f            d0f7                      BNE       COPY_REMAINDER_LOOP

                ; XREF[1]: 0791(j)

                ;**********************************************************************

                ;**********************************************************************

                ; READ_INPUT ($0806)

0a09            8523                      STA       TERM_DATA_PTR+1

                ;**********************************************************************
                ; PROCESS_TERM ($0A0E)
                ;
                ; Purpose: Interpret one compressed term stream with word wrapping until the '@' terminator.                 ; Inputs: TERM_DATA_PTR ($22/$23) points at the stream; CURRENT_COLUMN ($24) is the live column; UPPERCASE_LETTER_FLAG ($0AFF) selects capitalisation of the next letter.
                ; Outputs: The stream is rendered to the terminal with word wrapping and inter-word spaces; returns when the terminator is consumed.
                ; Assumptions: The wrap threshold is a hard-coded 41 ($29) compared against column plus word length. A word longer than forty characters would still overflow. The routine is re-entered recursively in effect through PROCESS_TOKEN, which saves and restores TERM_DATA_PTR on the stack.
                ; Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, WORD_REMAINING_LEN ($25), TERM_DATA_PTR, WORK_PTR ($0C/$0D), UPPERCASE_LETTER_FLAG, the terminal cursors and CURRENT_COLUMN.
                ; Hardware changes: Writes screen RAM at $CC00-$CFFF and colour RAM at $D800-$DBFF through PRINT_CHARACTER.
                ;**********************************************************************
PROCESS_TERM:
                ; XREF[8]: 09d4(c), 0a0b(c), 0a50(j), 0a54(j), 0a5b(j), 0bba(c), 1076(c), 1105(c)
0a0e            a901                      LDA       #0x1  ; WORD_REMAINING_LEN = 1

0a10            8525                      STA       WORD_REMAINING_LEN
0a12            a000                      LDY       #0x0

0a14            b122                      LDA       (TERM_DATA_PTR),Y  ; read next term byte
0a16            c940                      CMP       #0x40  ; '@' end of sentence?
                ; XREF from[1]: 0a18(j)
0a18            d001                      BNE       TOKEN_TEST
0a1a            60                        RTS
TOKEN_TEST:
                ; XREF[1]: 0a18(j)
0a1b            2980                      AND       #0x80  ; bit7 set -> token
                ; XREF from[1]: 0a1d(j)
0a1d            d054                      BNE       PROCESS_TOKEN
0a1f            c8                        INY             ; scan literal word, measuring its length

                ; XREF from[3]: 0a20(R), 0a20(R), 0a20(R)
0a20            b122                      LDA       (TERM_DATA_PTR),Y
0a22            c940                      CMP       #0x40  ; Sentence terminator

0a24            f038                      BEQ       TEST_WORD_FITS_SCREEN_2
0a26            c941                      CMP       #0x41  ; Before `a`?

0a28            9007                      BCC       CONTINUE_WORD_SCAN
0a2a            c95b                      CMP       #0x5b  ; Past `z`?

0a2c            b003                      BCS       CONTINUE_WORD_SCAN

0a2e            4c3b0a                    JMP       TEST_WORD_FITS_SCREEN_1

0a31            2980                      AND       #0x80
                ; XREF from[1]: 0a33(j)
0a33            d006                      BNE       TEST_WORD_FITS_SCREEN_1
                ; XREF from[1]: 0a35(RW)
0a35            e625                      INC       WORD_REMAINING_LEN  ; WORD_REMAINING_LEN++
0a37            c8                        INY

0a38            4c200a                    JMP       DISPATCH_CHARACTER
                ;**********************************************************************
                ; === TEST_WORD_FITS_SCREEN — wrap if the word won't fit, then print it ===
                ; If CURRENT_COLUMN + WORD_REMAINING_LEN >= $29 (41), emit a newline (PRINT_EMPTY_LINE) before
                ; printing the word (PRINT_WORD). Then TEST_ADD_SPACE adds a separating space unless the next
                ; char is a '.' or we're at column 0.
                ;**********************************************************************
TEST_WORD_FITS_SCREEN_1:
                ; XREF[2]: 0a2e(j), 0a33(j)
                ; XREF from[1]: 0a3b(R)
0a3b            a525                      LDA       WORD_REMAINING_LEN
0a3d            18                        CLC

0a3e            6524                      ADC       CURRENT_COLUMN  ; column + word length
0a40            c929                      CMP       #0x29  ; >= text width -> wrap
                ; XREF from[1]: 0a42(j)
0a42            9003                      BCC       CALL_PRINT_WORD

0a44            204b0b                    JSR       PRINT_EMPTY_LINE  ; newline

0a47            20db0a                    JSR       PRINT_WORD  ; print the word

                ; XREF[1]: 0ad8(j)
0a4a            a000                      LDY       #0x0
                ; XREF from[3]: 0a4c(R), 0a4c(R), 0a4c(R)
0a4c            b122                      LDA       (TERM_DATA_PTR),Y
0a4e            c92e                      CMP       #0x2e  ; next char '.'? -> no space

0a50            f0bc                      BEQ       PROCESS_TERM

0a52            a524                      LDA       CURRENT_COLUMN  ; If column 0, don't print a space
                ; XREF from[1]: 0a54(j)
0a54            f0b8                      BEQ       PROCESS_TERM
0a56            a920                      LDA       #0x20  ; add separating space
                ; XREF from[1]: 0a58(c)
0a58            20db08                    JSR       PRINT_CHARACTER
                ; XREF from[1]: 0a5b(j)
0a5b            4c0e0a                    JMP       PROCESS_TERM
TEST_WORD_FITS_SCREEN_2:
                ; XREF[1]: 0a24(j)
                ; XREF from[1]: 0a5e(R)
0a5e            a525                      LDA       WORD_REMAINING_LEN
0a60            18                        CLC
                ; XREF from[1]: 0a61(R)
0a61            6524                      ADC       CURRENT_COLUMN
0a63            c929                      CMP       #0x29  ; overflow screen?
                ; XREF from[1]: 0a65(j)
0a65            9003                      BCC       PRINT_WORD_AND_SPACE
                ; XREF from[1]: 0a67(c)
0a67            204b0b                    JSR       PRINT_EMPTY_LINE

                ; XREF from[1]: 0a6a(c)
0a6a            20db0a                    JSR       PRINT_WORD
0a6d            a920                      LDA       #0x20  ; Space
                ; XREF from[1]: 0a6f(c)
0a6f            20db08                    JSR       PRINT_CHARACTER
0a72            60                        RTS
                ;**********************************************************************
                ; === PROCESS_TOKEN — expand a compressed token (dictionary word) ===
                ; Token id has bit7 set; (id & $7F)*2 indexes TOKEN_POINTERS_BASE_ADDR ($25DD) to get a pointer
                ; to the token's text. Saves the current TERM_DATA_PTR, points it at the token text, PRINT_WORDs
                ; the expansion (capitalised if UPPERCASE_LETTER_FLAG), then restores TERM_DATA_PTR and resumes
                ; the sentence. Tokens encode frequently-used words to compress the text.
                ;**********************************************************************
PROCESS_TOKEN:

                ; XREF from[2]: 0a73(R), 0a73(R)
0a73            b122                      LDA       (TERM_DATA_PTR),Y

0a7d            297f                      AND       #0x7f  ; drop token bit7
0a7f            0a                        ASL       A     ; id * 2 (word table entries)

0a80            850c                      STA       WORK_PTR  ; Store processed token
                ; XREF from[1]: 0a82(j)
0a82            b007                      BCS       STORE_HIGH_BYTE  ; Can't reach, because `AND 7Fh` clears the high bit.
0a84            a900                      LDA       #0x0

0a86            850d                      STA       WORK_PTR+1

0a88            4c8f0a                    JMP       COMPUTE_TOKEN_ADDR

0a8b            a901                      LDA       #0x1

0a8d            850d                      STA       WORK_PTR+1

                ; XREF from[1]: 0a8f(R)

0a91            18                        CLC             ; Compute token address…

0a95            850c                      STA       WORK_PTR

0a99            6d681c                    ADC       TOKEN_POINTERS_BASE_ADDR+1

0aa2            8522                      STA       TERM_DATA_PTR  ; …and store into TERM_DATA_PTR
0aa4            c8                        INY

0aa5            b10c                      LDA       (WORK_PTR),Y
                ; XREF from[1]: 0aa7(W)
0aa7            8523                      STA       TERM_DATA_PTR+1
0aa9            a200                      LDX       #0x0
                ; XREF from[1]: 0aab(*)
0aab            a122                      LDA       (TERM_DATA_PTR,X)  ; token length (first byte)
                ; XREF from[1]: 0aad(W)
0aad            8525                      STA       WORD_REMAINING_LEN
0aaf            18                        CLC

0ab0            6524                      ADC       CURRENT_COLUMN
0ab2            c929                      CMP       #0x29  ; would overflow width? -> newline

0ab4            9003                      BCC       MOVE_POINTER_TO_CHARS

0ab6            204b0b                    JSR       PRINT_EMPTY_LINE

                ; XREF[1]: 0ab4(j)
                ; XREF from[1]: 0ab9(RW)
0ab9            e622                      INC       TERM_DATA_PTR  ; skip length byte -> token chars

0abf            a901                      LDA       #0x1

0ac1            8dff0a                    STA       UPPERCASE_LETTER_FLAG

                ; XREF from[1]: 0acf(j)

0ad8            4c4a0a                    JMP       TEST_ADD_SPACE
                ;**********************************************************************
                ; PRINT_WORD ($0ADB)
                ;
                ; Purpose: Emit the characters of one literal word or expanded token, applying the inline control codes: '.' prints a full stop and arms capitalisation, '<' emits a line break, $FF takes the following byte as a new text colour, and A-Z are folded to lowercase unless the capitalisation flag is set.
                ; Inputs: TERM_DATA_PTR ($22/$23) points at the first character; WORD_REMAINING_LEN ($25) is the character count; UPPERCASE_LETTER_FLAG ($0AFF) selects the case of the next letter.
                ; Outputs: The characters are printed, TERM_DATA_PTR is advanced past them, WORD_REMAINING_LEN reaches zero, and the capitalisation flag is cleared once it has been consumed.
                ; Assumptions: The $FF colour escape consumes one extra byte and decrements the length accordingly, so a stream that ends immediately after $FF would read past the word. Colour values are written straight to CURRENT_CHAR_COLOR without masking.
                ; Clobbers: A, X, flags, TERM_DATA_PTR, WORD_REMAINING_LEN, UPPERCASE_LETTER_FLAG, CURRENT_CHAR_COLOR ($0286), the terminal cursors and CURRENT_COLUMN.
                ; Hardware changes: Writes screen RAM at $CC00-$CFFF and colour RAM at $D800-$DBFF through PRINT_CHARACTER.

                ; XREF from[1]: 0b00(j)
0b00            f009                      BEQ       CONTINUE_LOWERCASE_LETTER

                ;**********************************************************************
                ; PRINT_EMPTY_LINE ($0B4B)

                ; Inputs: CURRENT_COLUMN ($24) and the terminal cursors.

                ; Assumptions: The loop is written as a self tail-jump rather than a counted loop, so it relies on PRINT_CHARACTER resetting the column exactly at 39.
                ; Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, the terminal cursors, CURRENT_COLUMN, and MEMCPY state if a scroll occurs.

PRINT_EMPTY_LINE:
                ; XREF[23]: 0439(c), 044a(c), 0810(c), 0813(c), 08d7(c), 099c(c), 0a44(c), 0a67(c),

0b57            60                        RTS
                ;**********************************************************************
                ; PRINT_ROOM_TEXT ($0B58)
                ;
                ; Purpose: Print one room description: convert the global room id to a part-relative index, resolve it through the room-text pointer table, emit two leading spaces, draw the first letter as a drop capital, then render the rest of the stream.
                ; Inputs: A = global room id. CURRENT_PART_NO ($2940) selects the base in PART_ROOM_BASE_IDS ($0DCC); the room-text pointer table base is the word at $2F00.
                ; Outputs: The room description printed with its two-by-two initial; TERM_DATA_PTR advanced past the leading letter. Tail-jumps to PROCESS_TERM.

                ;**********************************************************************
                ; ROOM_GRAPHIC_TABLE — 57 fixed six-byte room-illustration descriptors at $0BF9-$0D4E.
                ;
                ; RoomGraphicRecord layout, stride 6:
                ;   +0 start_row
                ;   +1 start_column
                ;   +2 source_ptr, little endian
                ;   +4 height_rows
                ;   +5 width_columns
                ;
                ; BLIT_ROOM_GRAPHIC copies these fields into zero-page blit state, then invokes COPY_BLIT_ROW three times per character row. Each source row is interleaved as width*8 bitmap bytes, width screen-matrix bytes, then width colour-RAM bytes. A record therefore consumes height*width*10 bytes. BITMAP_ROW_ADDR_TABLE, SCREEN_ROW_ADDR_TABLE, and COLOR_ROW_ADDR_TABLE select the ten destination rows in bitmap $E000, screen $CC00, and colour RAM $D800.
                ;
                ; The captured occupant uses descriptors 0-20. Descriptor 0 points to $A100; descriptors 1-20 form the current contiguous source chain $4300-$93E5 and are fully typed as ROOM_GFX_00 through ROOM_GFX_20. Descriptors 21-56 are resident transition metadata whose addressed payload occupants are absent from this capture; they remain structurally typed descriptors but are not expanded into noncaptured graphics.
                ;
                ; The 57-entry extent is established inside the capture: the following byte at $0D4F begins OBJ_ROOM_TABLE, that table's largest descriptor index is $38 (decimal 56), and a hypothetical descriptor at $0D4F has an impossible zero width.
                ;**********************************************************************

                ; COND_RANDOM ($1222)

                ; Purpose: Condition opcode $88: the engine's coin flip. Compares an operand threshold against the low eight bits of the VIC-II raster counter and returns the resulting carry, so the outcome depends on when in the frame the script happens to run.

                ;**********************************************************************
                ; PARSE_INPUT ($122F)
                ;
                ; Purpose: Turn one edited command line into an executed command. Splits the line into words and records their start and end offsets, then replaces each offset pair with a vocabulary token id, then resolves the verb and noun and dispatches the matching rule.
                ; Inputs: INPUT_TEXT_BUFFER ($CBA0) holds the lowercased line and INPUT_LEN ($26) its length. An empty line returns immediately.
                ; Outputs: PARSED_TOKENS ($28-$47) holds up to sixteen resolved token ids, WORD_COUNT ($27) the number of words, and the matching action script has been run, so any game state may have changed.
                ; Assumptions: The token table is sixteen two-byte slots and the tokenizer stops when it fills. Vocabulary matching uses only the first three characters of each word; the disambiguation block at $1325 inspects characters four to six to separate stems that share a prefix.
                ; Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, WORD_COUNT, PARSED_TOKENS, LOOP_COUNTER ($4B), SCRATCH_BYTE ($02), SCRATCH_INDEX ($03), SCRATCH_BYTE_2 ($04), WORD_BUFFER ($64-$69), MEMCPY_SOURCE ($0A/$0B), WORK_PTR ($0C/$0D), VERB_ID ($4C), NOUN_ID ($4D), SAVED_PARSE_INDEX ($6A), the self-modified operand at $13B1, and all VM and renderer state through dispatch.
                ; Hardware changes: None directly; the renderer writes screen and colour RAM, and an executed command may reach the disk and display paths.

                ;**********************************************************************
                ; RUN_SCRIPT ($1605)
                ;
                ; Purpose: The bytecode interpreter. A false condition skips forward to the next separator.
                ; Inputs: SCRIPT_PC ($4E/$4F) points at a script; the condition table base is the word at $1191 and the action table base is the word at $0DE1.
                ; Outputs: The script has been executed to its terminator, or control has left through one of the non-local exits ($0FC9, $0FDD, $0FF1). Any game state, display state or disk state may have changed.
                ; Assumptions: Both dispatches work by writing the handler address into the operand bytes of a JSR instruction ($1642/$1643 for conditions, $169A/$169B for actions), so the interpreter is self-modifying and not reentrant. When an action opcode of $80 or above is encountered in the action position, the interpreter backs SCRIPT_PC up by one and re-reads it as a condition.

                ;**********************************************************************
                ; GLOBAL_TURN_SCRIPT ($1C6F-$1CAF) - resident every-turn housekeeping bytecode, the first
                ; script PRINT_ROOM_DESCRIPTION runs ($148C) on each pass of MAIN_LOOP ($0409).
                ;
                ; This is interpreted data, not 6510 code. RUN_SCRIPT ($1605) walks it through SCRIPT_PC
                ; ($4E/$4F). Opcodes $80-$89 are conditions, dispatched through CONDITION_DISPATCH_TABLE
                ; ($1193); each returns carry, and a false condition jumps to the skip loop at $169F, so
                ; consecutive conditions AND together. Opcodes $00-$7F are actions via ACTION_DISPATCH_TABLE
                ; ($0DE3). $FE separates rules, $FF ends the script.
                ;
                ; What it does each turn:
                ;   - once only (OBJ_FLAGS[6]), sets Atreyu's strength OBJ_COUNTERS[1] = 50 and lights flag 7
                ;   - warns at strength 10 (sentence $1B) and kills at 0 (sentence $1C, pause, RESTART)
                ;   - grants OBJ_FLAGS[$11] while the Black Velvet Cape (object $1A) is carried
                ;   - keeps flag 7 set while the Glowglobe (object $13) is carried; flag 7 is the same "room
                ;     lit" flag DESCRIBE_CURRENT_ROOM ($107E) tests before printing anything
                ;   - counts turns in the dark in OBJ_COUNTERS[6] and kills at 4 (sentence $41)
                ;   - drains strength each turn while poisoned (OBJ_FLAGS[8], sentence $40)
                ;
                ; It ends with action $07 (RETURN_SKIP_CALLER), which pops the interpreter's self-modified JSR
                ; frame and returns straight to PRINT_ROOM_DESCRIPTION, so the trailing $FF is unreachable.
                ;
                ; Being below $2F00, it survives every part load: the PART1/2/3 overlays cover $2F00-$96FF
                ; only.
                ;**********************************************************************

                ;**********************************************************************
                ; TOKEN_POINTERS_TABLE — 94 little-endian pointers, one per compressed-text dictionary token.
                ; A prose byte with bit 7 set is a token reference: the renderer clears bit 7, doubles the
                ; remaining 0..93 id and reads the word at TOKEN_POINTERS_TABLE + 2*id. The pointer addresses a
                ; dictionary record, so ids $80-$DD are defined and $DE-$FF have no entry in this occupant.
                ; The 94 pointers occupy $25DD-$2698; the records they address begin immediately afterwards at
                ; $2699 (WORD_THE_LC) and run to $28B8.
                ;**********************************************************************

                ;**********************************************************************
                ; Compressed-text dictionary records, $2699-$28B8. Each record is one length byte followed by
                ; exactly that many ASCII characters, with no terminator and no padding; records are packed back
                ; to back and are reached only through TOKEN_POINTERS_TABLE ($25DD), never by scanning.
                ; The dictionary stores case-sensitive duplicates because prose is emitted verbatim: "the"
                ; ($2699) and "The" ($27CF), "to" ($26DB) and "To" ($2805), "There" ($26AB) and "there" ($2730),

                ; lower-case or capitalised member of such a pair.

9900             byte[1792]
                ;**********************************************************************
                ; ZERO_PAGE_BACKUP ($A000-$A0FF) - the game's shadow copy of zero page, swapped in and out
                ; around KERNAL calls by SWAP_ZERO_PAGE_AND_BACKUP ($053C).
                ;
                ; The game keeps its own working variables in zero page, which the KERNAL also uses. Rather
                ; than saving individual locations, $053C exchanges the two 256-byte images wholesale: for each
                ; index it loads the live byte, loads the backup byte, writes the backup value live, and writes
                ; the live value into the backup. One routine therefore serves both directions - calling it
                ; twice restores the original state - and there is no separate "restore" entry point.
                ;
                ;   053C  LDY #$FF
                ;   053E  LDA $0000,Y     ; live zero-page byte
                ;   0541  TAX
                ;   0542  LDA $A000,Y     ; corresponding backup byte
                ;   0545  STA $0000,Y     ; backup -> live
                ;   0548  TXA
                ;   0549  STA $A000,Y     ; live -> backup
                ;   054C  DEY
                ;   054D  CPY #$01        ; stop before index $01
                ;   054F  BNE $053E
                ;
                ; C64 SPECIFIC, AND THE REASON FOR THE ODD LOOP BOUND: the loop runs Y = $FF down to $02 and
                ; deliberately never touches $0000 and $0001. On a 6510 those two addresses are not RAM but the
                ; CPU's on-chip I/O port - $0001 is the bank-select register that decides whether BASIC, KERNAL,
                ; I/O or RAM is visible at $A000-$BFFF and $D000-$FFFF, and $0000 is its data-direction
                ; register. Swapping a stale value into $0001 would change the memory map underneath the
                ; running code, most likely unmapping the very routine performing the swap. Banking is managed
                ; separately, by explicit stores to $01 (see $975D, which restores the game's standard $36 map
                ; after a disk load).
                ;
                ; Note the backup lives at $A000-$BFFF RAM, i.e. underneath the BASIC ROM image, which is
                ; exactly the region the $01 value chosen by this game leaves as RAM.
                ;
                ; The instruction operands establish the $A000 base. Ghidra records an `abs,Y` reference one byte above the base, so operand inspection is required. Byte evidence agrees: aligning $A000 with $0000 matches 198 of 256 captured bytes, against 80 when aligned at $A001. The 58 differences are expected because the backup is a prior zero-page snapshot, not a live mirror.
                ;**********************************************************************
ZERO_PAGE_BACKUP:

                ;**********************************************************************
                ; ROOM_GFX_00 - ROOM_GRAPHIC_TABLE[0] source data, part 1. 8 rows x 14 columns blitted at
                ; character row 1, column 3; 1120 bytes = 8 * 14 * 10 (8 bitmap + 1 screen-code + 1 colour byte
                ; per character cell, interleaved one character row at a time).
                ;

                ; 1-20 it is not overwritten when a new part loads. See the plate at ROOM_GRAPHIC_TABLE ($0BF9)

ROOM_GFX_00:
a100             byte[1120]
                ;**********************************************************************
                ; OBJECT_ICON_TABLE ($A560-$BBDF, 5760 bytes) - 36 fixed 160-byte slots originally allocated
                ; to inventory and scripted-scene icons, laid out back to back with no header.
                ;
                ; ADDRESSING
                ; CALC_OBJECT_GRAPHIC_PTR ($0F70) computes the slot address as $A560 + $A0 * CURRENT_OBJECT_INDEX
                ; by repeated addition, leaving it in GRAPHIC_RECORD_PTR ($5A/$5B). For normal inventory icons the index is the position at which the resolver at $15E3 found the
                ; parsed noun key inside NOUN_TO_OBJECT_INDEX ($22A4). SCRIPT_SET_OBJECT_GRAPHIC ($113D) instead
                ; reads an icon index directly from action bytecode, so a scripted scene can select a slot that no
                ; parsed noun can reach. NOUN_TO_OBJECT_INDEX holds 36 entries before its $FF terminator at $22C8,
                ; and 36 * 160 = 5760 lands the last byte on $BBDF, immediately below SAVED_BITMAP ($BC00). Table
                ; extent and slot stride therefore corroborate each other.
                ;
                ; PAYLOAD FORMAT - identical to a RoomGraphicRecord payload with width = 4 cells and
                ; height = 4 character rows. The source stream is interleaved per character row:
                ;
                ;     32 bytes  bitmap      (4 cells x 8 scanlines)
                ;      4 bytes  screen matrix
                ;      4 bytes  colour RAM
                ;     ------------------------------------------------
                ;     40 bytes per character row, 4 rows = 160 bytes per icon
                ;
                ; BLIT_ROOM_GRAPHIC ($05BF) / COPY_BLIT_ROW ($0676) scatter those three spans to three different
                ; destinations, which is why they are interleaved rather than stored as three flat planes.
                ;
                ; C64 DISPLAY SEMANTICS (for a reader fluent in 6510 but not in VIC-II)
                ; The picture band runs in multicolor bitmap mode: RASTER_SPLIT_PICTURE ($A7E3) sets $D011=$3B
                ; (BMM=1, bitmap mode), $D016=$D8 (MCM=1, multicolor), $D018=$38 (video matrix $CC00, bitmap
                ; $E000, both inside VIC bank 3) and $D021=$00. In that mode the VIC consumes TWO bitmap bits per
                ; pixel, so horizontal resolution halves - each 8x8 cell is 4 double-wide pixels across - and the
                ; colour of a pixel is selected by the bit pair:
                ;
                ;     00 -> background register $D021
                ;     01 -> high nybble of that cell's screen-matrix byte
                ;     10 -> low  nybble of that cell's screen-matrix byte
                ;     11 -> low  nybble of that cell's colour-RAM byte
                ;
                ; Hence the 4 screen bytes and 4 colour bytes per row: they carry three of the four palette
                ; entries for the four cells in that row. An icon is 32 x 32 screen pixels (16 double-wide
                ; multicolor pixels wide).
                ;
                ; WHERE THEY ARE DRAWN
                ; VISIBLE_OBJECT_RECORDS ($2943) is six 6-byte RoomGraphicRecords, all with height=4 width=4, at
                ; (row 0, col 21), (0,28), (0,35), (5,21), (5,28), (5,35) - a 3x2 inventory grid to the right of
                ; the room illustration, which occupies columns 3-16. SHOW_OBJECT_ICON ($0F3A) scans those six
                ; records for one whose source_ptr high byte is zero, writes the computed icon address into it,
                ; and calls RENDER_ROOM_GRAPHICS ($0570) to repaint the band.
                ;
                ; SCRIPTED, UNUSED, AND OVERWRITTEN SLOTS
                ; Part 1's NOUN_TO_OBJECT_INDEX holds 0 at positions 4, 5, 23, 24, 27, 29, 30 and 31. Because
                ; the normal noun resolver searches linearly and position 0 legitimately holds key 0 (noun "aur"
                ; = AURYN), a later zero cannot be selected through ordinary parsed-noun resolution. This does
                ; not make every such graphics slot dead: action opcode $17 reads the following byte as a slot
                ; index directly.
                ;
                ; Slot 23 is Falkor. Dynamic execution of "get falkor" in part 1 at room $21 selected verb-rule
                ; pair 14 and ACTION_SCRIPT_GET_FALKOR; bytes $17,$17 at $2B8F-$2B90 made
                ; SCRIPT_SET_OBJECT_GRAPHIC cache index $17 and COPY_BLIT_ROW read from $B3C0.
                ;
                ; Slot 24 is Artax. Vocabulary entry "art" has noun id $57, VERB_RULE_GET_ARTAX is pair 13
                ; ($15,$57), its pointer selects ACTION_SCRIPT_GET_ARTAX at $2B55, and that script's successful
                ; room-$25 branch contains $17,$18 at $2B5E-$2B5F. The horse artwork therefore has a direct,
                ; unambiguous code identity even though it is not selected by ordinary noun-to-icon mapping.
                ;
                ; Slot 27 is unused crucifix artwork. The image is a Latin cross and vocabulary entry "cru" has
                ; noun id $5A, but the corresponding resolver key $28 is absent from NOUN_TO_OBJECT_INDEX.
                ; CURRENT_OBJECT_INDEX has only two writers: the noun resolver at $15FB and direct script action
                ; $17 at $114F. No action bytecode contains the required direct pair $17,$1B, and no decoded instruction or recorded reference reads $B640-$B6DF. The artwork is resident,
                ; recognisable abandoned content, not a live part-specific remap.
                ;
                ; The build reuses otherwise unreachable slot ranges:
                ;
                ;     slot  4  $A7E0-$A87F  active gameplay raster handlers through $A847; artwork tail at $A848
                ;     slot  5  $A880-$A91F  excluded intro IRQ bytes through $A892, active system-handoff
                ;                           routines through $A8DE, and artwork tail at $A8DF
                ;     slots 29-31 $B780-$B95F  excluded intro data through $B906 and artwork tail at $B907
                ;
                ; The exact boundaries $A7E0 = $A560 + 4*160 and $B780 = $A560 + 29*160 corroborate the slot arithmetic. The excluded intro occupants are retained only as typed bytes.
                ;
                ; Decoding each 160-byte slot with the interleaved multicolor rule above yields 36 recognisable
                ; adventure objects, and they match the game's own three-letter noun stems: slot 0 (noun key $00,
                ; object id $32, stem "aur") renders as the two-serpent AURYN amulet; "kni" is a dagger, "web" a
                ; spider web, "dia" a faceted diamond, "app" an apple, "coi" a coin, and so on. Verified against
                ; the retained gameplay image over $0000-$CFFF apart from the CPU port at $0000/$0001.
                ;**********************************************************************

                ; Purpose: The gameplay interrupt handler, installed in the KERNAL RAM vector CINV. A CLC followed by a BCC whose offset byte at $A7E2 is self-modified selects one of the three raster-split phase bodies, so successive interrupts cycle picture, text and bottom.

                ; Outputs: The selected phase reprograms the VIC, arms the next raster compare, rewrites the offset byte for the following interrupt, acknowledges the VIC interrupt latch and chains to the KERNAL epilogue at $EA81, which pulls the registers and executes RTI.
                ; Assumptions: Requires $01=$36 or another configuration in which $A000-$BFFF reads as RAM; banking BASIC back in while this vector is live would vector the interrupt into ROM.                 ; Inputs: Entered from the dispatcher with offset $00, on the interrupt armed for raster line 49. The KERNAL register-save frame is present.

                ; Inputs: Entered from the dispatcher with offset $27, on the interrupt armed for raster line 130. The KERNAL register-save frame is present.

                ;**********************************************************************
                ; RESTORE_SYSTEM_TO_BASIC ($A893)
                ;
                ; Purpose: Hand the machine back to the KERNAL and BASIC ROMs in a state a stock C64 can survive: select a ROM-visible memory map, zero the low RAM pages, rebuild the KERNAL indirect vector block, re-run BASIC's vector and zero-page initialisation, and restore the stock IRQ handler.
                ; Inputs: None. Physically located inside a dead object-icon slot, which is why it survives in the icon table region.
                ; Outputs: $01 = $36; $0002-$0101, $0200-$02FF and $0300-$03FF zeroed (the STA $0002,Y loop runs Y=$00..$FF, so it spills two bytes into the stack page); $B2/$B3 = $033C (the cassette-buffer pointer) and $C2 = 3; the 32-byte KERNAL default vector table copied from $FD30 to $0314-$0333; BASIC's indirect vectors and zero page reinitialised through KERNAL $E453 and $E3BF; CINV ($0314/$0315) = $EA31.
                ; Assumptions: $01 must be set first, because everything afterwards reads KERNAL ROM. Note the consequence for its own neighbourhood: with $36 selected, $A000-$BFFF still reads as RAM, so this code and the icon table around it remain reachable, while $E000-$FFFF is ROM, which is why the game's own character set at $F800 becomes invisible to the CPU though the VIC-II still sees it. No resident caller is recorded in the captured occupant.
                ; Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, the whole of zero page and pages 2 and 3, and BASIC's workspace. X is destroyed by the KERNAL calls to $E453 and $E3BF.
                ; Hardware changes: Writes the 6510 port $01. Rewrites the KERNAL RAM vector block $0314-$0333 including CINV. Calls KERNAL $E453 and $E3BF.                 ; INSTALL_GAME_IRQ ($A8CC)
                ;
                ; Purpose: Point the KERNAL RAM interrupt vector at the game's raster-split dispatcher and stop CIA 1 from raising its own interrupt. The exact inverse of the tail of RESTORE_SYSTEM_TO_BASIC.
                ; Inputs: None. Also located inside a dead object-icon slot.
                ; Outputs: CINV ($0314/$0315) = $A7E0; CIA 1's FLAG interrupt mask cleared; any latched CIA 1 interrupt request discarded.
                ; Assumptions: Requires $01=$36 so that $A7E0 is the game's handler in RAM rather than BASIC ROM, and requires the raster source and initial compare to have been configured already.                 ; Clobbers: A and flags.
